title: Failsafe streaming negotiation, backoff windows, and toolcall idempotency for OpenAI adapter
author: Aisha Banerjee
release_notes: Added a failsafe negotiation layer to the OpenAI compatibility adapter: client cancel + resume semantics with bounded backoff; ephemeral resume token rotation; server-side soft/hard cancel windows; toolcall idempotency markers to make function calls robust across reconnects; minor header additions for resume support. No public API surface changes beyond optional headers and compatible error mappings.
commits: feat(adapter): add negotiation state machine for resume/cancel with backoff windows
fix(test): stabilize TestResumeRace by using deterministic clock
feat(toolcall): add idempotency token handling and replay guard
docs: document X-Redwood-Resume-Token header and expected error mappings
ci: add e2e pipeline harness for flaky network scenarios
description:
Motivation: Customers and partner integrations have reported hard failures during transient network disconnects (mobile clients, flaky proxies) when using the OpenAI-compatible streaming endpoints. Existing behavior either drops in-flight tool calls or returns partial structured output that clients cannot reconcile. This PR introduces a failsafe negotiation layer in the OpenAI compatibility adapter to make the streaming lifecycle resilient while remaining backwards-compatible.

What this changes: Implement a Negotiator that tracks ephemeral resume leases and supports: bounded rejoin windows (soft cancel -> hard deadline), exponentially bounded client backoff hints, and rotation of a short-lived X-Redwood-Resume-Token header that clients may present to resume an in-flight stream. The server surface maps internal lease states to OpenAI-compatible status patterns (we return 409 Conflict when resume token mismatches, 410 Gone when hard deadline elapsed, and keep 200/stream for normal flows).

Key behaviors: 1) Soft cancel: when a client issues a cancel, we mark the stream as soft-cancelled and keep tool call side effects reversible/compensatable for the configured grace window (default 30s). 2) Resume: clients that reconnect with a valid X-Redwood-Resume-Token within the soft window are reattached and receive the remaining stream; tool/function calls are either guaranteed idempotent (via idempotency tokens) or replay-guarded by server-side dedup markers. 3) Hard deadline: after the hard deadline (configurable, default 120s) we GC session state and any subsequent resume attempts return 410. 4) Backoff hints: negotiator emits a Retry-After-like suggestion using a shim header X-Redwood-Resume-Backoff to guide client reconnection pacing (helps avoid thundering herd on large-scale reconnects).

Compatibility notes: The OpenAI adapter exposes the behavior using optional headers and light-weight error codes; no changes to the core generation payload format. Existing clients that do not send resume tokens will continue to observe the current cancel semantics (immediate cancel). The new headers are purely opt-in.

Testing and validation: Added unit tests for the negotiator state transitions and toolcall dedupe. An e2e CI pipeline simulates flaky networks (TCP close, partial frames, delayed reconnect) and validates that structured JSON boundaries remain parseable and that function-call side effects are either executed once or rolled back according to configured policies. The flaky TestResumeRace was stabilized by switching to a deterministic test clock and adding explicit wait points.

Operational considerations: Metrics added: negotiator.resume.attempts, negotiator.resume.success, negotiator.resume.expired, negotiator.soft_cancel.count, negotiator.hard_deadline.gc_count and toolcall.dedupe.hits. Alerts suggested: spike in resume.expired or GC rate -> investigate long-lived clients or clock skew.

Migration: Platform teams using private deployments can tune soft/hard windows via operator flags in the private installer; hosted customers will see sane defaults. No forced migration required.

Files of interest and high-level diffs: negotiator.go - new state machine (~300 LOC) with clear state diagram in comments; idempotency.go - server-side dedupe map with TTL and optional persistent store hook; adapter.go - wiring to attach negotiator to streaming request lifecycle and header parsing; docs/headers.md - documents X-Redwood-Resume-Token and X-Redwood-Resume-Backoff and error mappings; examples/js/resume-client.js - minimal client demonstrating disconnect/rejoin flow; ci/e2e/streaming_resilience.yml - CI job that runs network-chaos scenarios.

Implementation notes: Negotiator is intentionally conservative: default windows favor safety over resource retention. Toolcall idempotency uses a two-phase guard: client-provided idempotency key + server-assigned replay token to tolerate client re-sends across disconnects. The replay token is rotated on every successful resume to avoid indefinite reuse.

Risks and mitigations: 1) Resource retention for GC windows - mitigated by hard deadline and tenant-level caps. 2) Complexity surfaced to client via headers - mitigated by keeping headers optional and providing example clients. 3) Edge-case races between toolcall execution and resume - mitigated by server-side replay guards and test coverage.

Future work: expose per-route resume policies, integrate with Dedicated capacity routing to prefer local-zone resume, and add a monitoring dashboard in Redwood Console for resume metrics.

notes_for_release: Operators: this feature is off by default in older private installer releases; check private-installer flags `negotiator.soft_window` and `negotiator.hard_window`. Hosted users: no action required. SDK teams: example client added in redwood-openai-compat/examples/js/resume-client.js — consider copying into language SDKs if you want resume support.
egress_examples: Error mapping: 409 -> resume token conflict (client should fetch new token or start fresh)
Error mapping: 410 -> session expired (hard deadline passed)
Client flow: send resume token on reconnect, wait for 200/stream and continue consuming
